sections.html:
Franklin County handles property tax from the Government Annex Building at 901 Public Square in Benton, the county seat. A single number, 618-435-9800, reaches the Treasurer, the Supervisor of Assessments and the Board of Review. Offices keep weekday hours from eight in the morning to four in the afternoon.

  • Treasurer: collects the bill, takes mail at PO Box 967, Benton, IL 62812, and runs the delinquent tax sale
  • Supervisor of Assessments: the chief county assessment officer, who handles exemptions and mailing address changes
  • Board of Review: three county citizens appointed by the County Board, with the chief assessment officer as clerk
  • County Clerk: explains how to pay delinquent taxes after a sale

Township assessors set the starting values. The county has assessors for Goode/Barren, Benton, Browning, Cave/Eastern, Denning, Ewing/Northern, Frankfort, Six Mile and Tyrone, so phone the assessment office to find out who covers your parcel.

Two numbers drive the bill: the value your township assessor puts on the property, and the money your local taxing districts say they need for the coming year. The assessment office likens it to income tax, a rate applied to a base.

Roughly 60% of what's collected goes to education. The rest is divided among the county, cities, park districts, library districts, fire districts, townships and other special districts, more than fifty local governments in all. The school district where the property sits takes the biggest share.

Assessments can drop while rates climb, since a rate depends on the district's total levy and its total equalized assessed value. The Treasurer's page posts a rate report for 2025 taxes payable in 2026, and your own bill shows the rate for each of your taxing districts.

A parcel inside a tax increment finance district works differently. Taxes on growth above the "TIF Base" flow to the TIF fund rather than the other taxing bodies. The Treasurer gives the formula as (Net Taxable Value minus TIF Base) times the Tax Rate. The county doesn't create TIF districts or control how the money is spent.

sections.h2: Late penalties and the tax sale
sections.html:
Illinois law has the collector add a 1.5% penalty for each month an installment is late, and an installment is timely only if paid on or before its due date. Unpaid tax goes to the annual tax sale.

Franklin County tax and appeal rules at a glance
RuleAmount or timing
Late payment penalty1.5% per month on each late installment
Tax buyer interest, first yearInitial maximum rate of 18%
Tax buyer interest, later yearsInitial rate of 12% on subsequent years' taxes the buyer pays
Board of Review startConvenes the first Monday in June
Complaint window30 calendar days after the assessment list is published
Evidence for unequal treatment5 comparable properties with size, age and condition

Bidders at the sale pay the taxes and penalties, then charge the owner interest. If the owner doesn't repay the buyer in the allowed time, the buyer may ask a court for a deed. Separately, the county takes sealed bids on real estate and mobile homes it has acquired for delinquent taxes, and a delinquent tax agent runs a yearly sale of those parcels.

You can begin with the township assessor or go straight to the Board of Review, and each has its own time frame. The Board accepts complaints in writing, on its own forms, signed and showing the property address, within 30 calendar days after the assessment list is published for the year in question.

Put all your evidence in with the original complaint, since the Board looks only at what it receives. A claim of overvaluation needs proof such as an appraisal. A claim of unequal treatment needs five comparable properties nearby, with square footage, age and condition for each.

If the Board's ruling doesn't satisfy you, the next stop is the Illinois Property Tax Appeal Board. The Treasurer adds that a taxpayer with a dispute left after the complaint process can go to circuit court, but has to keep paying the billed tax meanwhile to avoid tax liens. Keep a copy of everything you file.

Most exemptions require a residential home that the taxpayer owns and lives in. The Supervisor of Assessments lists these programs:

  • General homestead exemption for owner-occupied single-family homes
  • Senior citizens homestead exemption for owners 65 and older
  • Senior assessment freeze, which needs Form PTAX-340 filed every year
  • Homestead improvement exemption, covering four years after an improvement is finished and occupied
  • Disabled persons exemption, filed on PTAX-343 and renewed each year with PTAX-343-R
  • Disabled veteran standard and homestead exemptions
  • Returning veteran exemption, on Form PTAX-341

Dollar amounts change nearly every year, so ask the assessment office for current figures. Only the general homestead and senior homestead exemptions skip annual renewal. Seniors can also use the county's real estate tax deferral through the Treasurer, which places a lien on the home and is repaid when it sells or transfers. The state's Circuit Breaker grant is applied for through the Illinois Department of Revenue.

sections.h2: Franklin County housing at a glance
sections.html: Franklin County is in Southern Illinois. Benton is the seat, and West Frankfort is the largest city. Population is 36,916 and there are 18,461 housing units. The median owner-occupied home is valued at $89,000, and 74.1% of housing units are owner-occupied. Median household income is $56,740 and median gross rent is $803. Building activity is slow, with just 19 permits issued in 2025.

The bill is mailed to the owner at the address on the deed. In a typical transaction the seller credits the buyer for real estate taxes at closing, and the two sides work that out between them.

Here's a sensible order of steps before you close:

  • Call the Treasurer for installment dates and the amount still owed on the parcel, since the bill itself carries the exact figures.
  • If taxes are unpaid, clear them before the sale date, because a delinquent house can be in line for the tax sale.
  • If the bill goes to an old address, return the county's change of address form to the Supervisor of Assessments.
  • Give the title company the exact balance so the closing statement is right.

Nothing in the county's process bars a sale while tax is owed. A cash sale just means the balance gets settled from proceeds at closing, without a lender's payoff step.

faqs.q: Where do I pay property tax in Franklin County, Illinois?
faqs.a: Pay the Franklin County Treasurer at the Government Annex Building, 901 Public Square in Benton, or by mail to PO Box 967. The office phone is 618-435-9800, and the county website has a real estate tax inquiry link.

faqs.q: What is the late penalty for Franklin County property tax?
faqs.a: It's 1.5% per month on each late installment, as Illinois law requires. An installment is on time only if it's paid by its due date, and unpaid tax can be sold at the annual tax sale.

faqs.q: How much interest can a Franklin County tax buyer charge?
faqs.a: A winning bidder at the tax sale charges the owner interest at an initial maximum rate of 18%. If the buyer pays later years' taxes too, the initial rate on those is 12%.

faqs.q: Who hears assessment complaints in Franklin County?
faqs.a: The Board of Review, which has three citizen members appointed by the County Board. Complaints are due within 30 calendar days after the assessment list is published, and Board rulings can be appealed to the Illinois Property Tax Appeal Board.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Franklin County house if the tax is unpaid?
faqs.a: Yes. Buyer and seller settle the tax at closing, and nothing bars a sale. Call the Treasurer for the exact balance first so the closing statement carries the right figure.
